# Galadon
A five-stage engineering loop for agent-built projects.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Galadon initializes a small engineering workspace, then keeps the agent on one
phase at a time. The

core knows only phases, artifacts and gates. Everything
else is a port:
| Port | Purpose | Reference implementation |

| `RolePort` | Who does the work | `solo` |
| `TemplatePort` | Which `docs/profile.md` to write; the

code skeleton comes from `--layout`/`--stack` | `web`, `api`, `static` |
| `DeployPort` | How to bu
ild, migrate, release, probe and roll back | `local`, `ssh` |

The bundled implementations are examples. A project can replace any port
without changing the five-s

d implementations are examples. A project can replace any port
without changing the five-stage loop.
## Install

The plugin ships the skill and the CLI together; no separate install step is
needed.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Inside a workspace the agent runs the bundled `bin/galadon`. To use the CLI
yourself, either call `b
in/galadon` from the plugin directory or install it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Requires Python 3.10+ and `PyYAML`.
## Quick start
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then let the agent drive: it reads `galadon.yaml`, does the current phase, and
runs `galadon check`

until the loop reaches `learn`. With the default `none`
layout the first gate is the spec: `init` wr

ites a `spec/spec.md` stub full of
TODO, so `check` fails with "spec/spec.md still contains TODO" un

til you write
it. `init` also leaves `checks.build` and `checks.test` empty on purpose, so
once the

spec is done `check` fails loudly with "no checks configured — declare
checks.build/checks.test" unt

il you declare the real commands. A non-`none`
layout ships a filled-in spec and real checks instead
(see Layouts below).
## Layouts

`init --layout` adds the inside-project layering shared by the production
projects this scaffold was

sampled from. The default
`none` keeps 0.2.x behaviour: base template only, no layout contract.
| Layout | Use it for | Creates |

| `none` (default) | a bare Galadon loop | base template only |
| `webapp` | a product with a backen
d and a frontend | `server/`, `src/` (python stack), `web/`, `e2e/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, `deploy/`
, `openspec/`, `spec/{spec.md,INDEX.md,TESTING.md,CONSTITUTION.md,domains/}`, `wiki/{knowledge,progr

ess,runbook}/`, `.agents/`, `config.md` |
| `service` | a backend service or scheduled job | `server
/`, `src/` (python stack), `tests/`, `scripts/`, `deploy/`, `openspec/`, `spec/{spec.md,INDEX.md,TES
TING.md,CONSTITUTION.md,domains/}`, `wiki/{knowledge,progress,runbook}/`, `.agents/`, `config.md` |
| `plugin` | a distributable agent plugin | `bin/<project>`, `src/<project>/`, `skills/<project>/`,
`docs/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, `openspec/`, `spec/{spec.md,INDEX.md,TESTING.md,CONSTITUTION.md,domai
ns/}`, `wiki/{knowledge,progress,runbook}/`, `.agents/`, `config.md` |

The `python` stack adds a `src/<package>/` code root; the `node` stack puts the
entry in `server/ind

ex.js` (`webapp`, `service`) or `src/index.js` (`plugin`), so
`webapp` and `service` have no `src/`

ebapp`, `service`) or `src/index.js` (`plugin`), so
`webapp` and `service` have no `src/` on `node`.

Every non-`none` layout also carries the spec truth layer under `spec/`:
`INDEX.md` (the living feat

ure index), `domains/README.md` (one behaviour
contract per domain), `TESTING.md` (the change-to-che

ck trigger matrix), and
`CONSTITUTION.md` (the hard rules). These four files live once in
`templates

/layouts/_shared/` and render before the layout's own `common/`
layer, so a layout can override a fi

le while `none` stays unchanged. The files
every layout shares byte for byte (the `.agents/` slots a

nd READMEs, the
`wiki/`, `openspec/` and `scripts/` READMEs, `.gitignore` and
`openspec/config.yaml`

) live there once too; `plugin` keeps its own versions of
the ones that differ.
`--stack` picks the code skeleton and the real checks:
| Stack | build | test |

## Remote deploys

`deploy.adapter: ssh` ships a directory to a host that runs systemd and a
reverse proxy, with releas

es, an atomic `current`/`previous` switch, a deploy
lock and a commit-versioned JSON probe:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`bootstrap` creates the system user, release tree, systemd unit and a marked
reverse-proxy block (it

backs the proxy config up and validates before
reloading). `teardown --yes` only removes a root tha

t still carries the
`bootstrap` marker.

`deploy.adapter: local` uses the same release tree under
`deploy.options.root` (default `.galadon/de

ploy`):
`releases/<timestamp>-<version>`, an atomic `current` switch, a retained
`previous`, and `sh

ared/deploy.lock`. A held lock refuses the ship; a failed
probe restores `current` to `previous`, re

-probes that release and exits
non-zero with the live release named.
## Side effects
Read this before pointing it at a machine you care about.

- `bootstrap` writes on the remote host: a system user (unless
`options.manage_user: false`), `<remo

te_root>/{releases,shared}`, a systemd
unit, and one marked block in the reverse-proxy config. The p

roxy config is
backed up first and validated before any reload; a failed validation restores
it and

does not reload.
- `ship` writes an immutable release, switches `current` atomically and keeps
`prev

ious`; the `ssh` adapter also restarts the service. It then probes the
release. A failed probe rolls

back to `previous`, re-probes it and exits
non-zero.
- `teardown --yes` removes the unit, the marke

d proxy block, the release tree
and the system user, but only if the root still carries the `bootstr

ap`
marker.
- Every remote write prints its target first. `--env prod` additionally
requires `--yes-
prod` in the same invocation.
## Limits

- `DeployPort` implementations: `local` and `ssh` (systemd + Caddy). `k8s` is a
declared port with n

o implementation; calling it fails loudly.
- The `ssh` adapter assumes root access (or an account th

at can write the unit
and the proxy config), `rsync`, `flock` and `systemctl` on the target.
- The p

roxy block uses a Caddy snippet named `access_log`; hosts without that
